“Chachnama” was translated to Persian by
o: Muhammad Ali Bin Abu Bakr Kufi
More than one of the above
x: The Persian translation of Chachnama was done by Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi. Chachnama is a book written in the Arabic language, but there is no clear information available about the author of this book. Chachnama describes the history of Sindh from 680 to 718 A.D. The complete translation of this book from Persian to English was done in 1900 A.D. by Mirza Kalich Beg.

s: The first Muslim invaders of India were –
x: The very first successful Muslim invasion of India took place in Sindh in the year 712 A.D by the Arabs under the leadership of Muhammad-Bin-Qasim. He displaced Raja Dahir, who ruled Sindh from his capital, Arod (near modern Karachi).

s: Muhammad-Bin-Qasim was a –
x: Muhammad-Bin-Qasim was an Arab ruler born around 695 A.D. He was the nephew and son-in-law of Iraq’s King Al- Hajjaj. At the age of seventeen, he was sent by Caliph-al- Walid to lead an army to Sindh (India). 9. According to Chachnama, what was the Capital of the Indus Country in the 6th and 7th century? (a) Deval (b) Arod (c) Lodawa (d) Barmer M.P.P.C.S. (Pre.) 2020 Ans (b) Chachnama ("Story of Chach") is one of the main historical sources for the history of Sindh in the 7th to 8th century A.D, written in Arabic. It takes its name from Raja Chach of Sindh whose son Dahir stood against Muhammad Bin Qasim's invasion of Sindh in 8th Century A.D. Text states that Arod served as capital of the Indus country in the 6th and 7th century A.D. Hence option (b) is correct.

s: Who was the Hindu King at the time of invasion of Muhammad-bin-Qasim on Sindh?
x: Muhammad bin Qasim removed Raja Dahir, ruler of Sindh with his capital at Alor, so Dahir is the answer.

s: When did the first contact of India with Islam established?
o: After the arrival of Sufi Saints
In the 11th century after establishment of Turkish rule in India.
In the 7th century after conquest of sindh by Muhammad-bin-Qasim.
Arrival of Arab traders on the Malabar Coast.
x: The notes do not mention Arab traders on the Malabar Coast. The notes link Islam's first arrival to Sindh in 712, but the answer keyed here is the Arab traders' contact.

s: Who was Muhammad bin Qasim?
x: Muhammad bin Qasim led the Arab invasion of Sindh in 712, so he was an Arab, not a Turk or Mongol.

s: Which among the following were first Muslim Invader in India?
x: The Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim (712) were the first Muslim invaders of India, before the Ghaznavids and Ghurids.

s: First Muslim attack on India occurred in the year
x: King Dahir of Sindh fought the battle with Muhammad-Bin- Qasim, the first successful Muslim invader who defeated Dahir in this battle. He arrived at the coast of Sindh in 712 A.D. (Now in Pakistan) and was successful in defeating and killing Dahir. Note : There is a dispute about the exact date of the first successful Muslim invasion of India. According to V.D. Mahajan, this date is 711 A.D. but according to Harish Chandra Verma, this date is 712 A.D.

s: First Muslim invader in India was
x: The first successful Muslim invader of India was Muhammad- Bin-Qasim. In the beginning of the 8th century A.D., under the leadership of Muhammad Bin-Qasim, a part of India was unsuccessfully attacked. The empire of Arabs couldn’t spread towards the east of Sindh and Multan, and it gradually declined. In the words of Dr. Stanley Lane-Poole “Although Arabs conquered Sindh, but it remained only an episode in history of India and Islam. This was an incomplete victory”. Their incomplete task was done by Turks.

s: The Famous king in Yadavaraja Dynasty?
After the attack of Mahmud Ghazni, who among the following reconstructed the Somnath temple?
x: Bhimadeva was the ruler during the attack of Mahmud Gazhani on Somnath Temple (1025/26 AD). After Gazhani left with the loot of Somnath, Bhimadeva-I reconstructed the temple.

s: Which of the following Chandela Kings was not defeated by Mahmud Ghaznavi –
x: The Chandela dynasty is famous in Indian history for the King Vidyadhar, who repulsed the attacks of Mahmud Ghaznavi during 1019-20 A.D. From the ninth century to the 13th century, the Chandelas ruled over Central India. Their first capital city was Khajuraho, which was later shifted to Mahoba.

s: Who among the following was the founder of Ghaznavid dynasty?
x: Towards the end of the ninth century, Trans-oxiana, Khurasan and parts of Iran were being ruled by the Samanids who were Iranian by descent. Among the Samanid governors there was a Turkish Slave, Alptigin, who, in course of time, established an independent kingdom with its capital at Ghazni and founded Ghaznavid dynasty, which soon took over the control of Samanid Kingdom.

s: Who among the following issued silver coins with Sanskrit legend on one side:
x: The silver coins introduced by Mahmud Ghazni were struck in India with Arabic and Sanskrit inscriptions on it.

s: Which among the following Indian ruler was not defeated by Mahmud Ghaznavi?
What was the main motive of Mahmud Ghaznavi in context of invasion of India?
o: To make the country its colony.
x: Mahmud raided for plunder and temple wealth and did not seek a permanent empire, so plunder was his main motive.

s: Who fought the Battle of Waihind (AD 1009)?

s:

x: Turkish conqueror Mahmud of Ghazni succeeded his father in 998 A.D. He established a huge empire in Central Asia with it's capital at Ghazni (Afghanistan). For 17 times, he attacked India from 1000 to 1027 A.D. He was a ruthless invader and plunderer of wealth. In these invasions, his aim was not to establish any permanent Muslim rule in India but to take away the huge wealth of the country.

s: Who was the court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni –
x: Mahmud of Ghazni was just a plunderer who mounted at least 17 raids in India. But in his kingdom in Afghanistan, he had shown love for art and culture. He patronized three persons: i. Firdausi (Persian Poet, known as Homer of the East) who wrote Shahnama. ii. Albiruni (a brilliant scholar from Central Asia) who wrote Tahqiq-I-Hind. iii. Utbi (court historian), who wrote Kitab-ul-Yamni and Tarikh-i-Yamini.

s: Which one of the following statements about Alberuni is not correct?
o: His writing was influenced by India
He was an expert of trigonometry
x: Al-Biruni was born in 973 A.D. in the territory of Khwarizm, now called Khiva, in Central Asia. He was not a secular writer because Al-biruni never gave any sympathetic reference to the contemporary event of Somnath temple raid by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025/1026.

s: Farista, the author of Shah-nama was associated with the court of
x: The notes do not mention Farista. The Shahnama was written by Firdausi at Mahmud of Ghazni's court, so the answer is Mahmud Ghazanavi.

s: Al-Biruni came with Mahmud Ghaznavi in?
x: Al-Biruni came with Mahmud of Ghazni, who raided India in 1000-1027, so he came in the 11th century AD.

s: Who among the following has wrote Kitab-ul-Hind or Tahkik-e-Hind?
x: Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind) was written by Al-Biruni, who was in Mahmud's court.

s: Who was the famous author of Kitab ul-Hind?
x: Al-Biruni, scholar at Mahmud of Ghazni's court, wrote Kitab-ul-Hind. Hasan Nizami and Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote other chronicles (Taj-ul-Maasir, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri).

s: Al-Beruni came to India in –
x: Al-Biruni came with Mahmud of Ghazni and described 11th-century India, so he came in the 11th century CE (Mahmud's raids were 1000-1027).

s: The famous historian who visited India with Mahmud of Ghazni was –
x: During 11th century A.D. Al-Biruni, the father of Indian Historical writing accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India and stayed here for many years. Al-Biruni translated Patanjali’s Yoga-Sutra into Arabic (called Kitab Patanjal) but Tahqiq-I-Hind (Reality of Hindustan) was his most important work in which he gave a socio-cultural description of India.

s: Whom had Muhammad Ghori defeated in 1194 in the Battle of Chandawar?
x: At Chandawar in 1194 Ghori defeated Jaichand (Jayachandra) of Kannauj, the Gahadavala king.

s: Which one of the following kings was defeated by Muhammad Ghori in the battle of Chandawar?

s: Who among the following rules is famous as “Prithvi Raj Chauhan”?
x: Ruler of Ajmer, Prithviraja-III, commonly known as Prithviraj Chauhan, defeated Muhammad Ghori in the first battle of Tarain in 1191 AD but faced defeat in the second battle of Tarain, in 1192 AD. 2. The brave Chauhan ruler of Ajmer who conquered Delhi and annexed it into his kingdom was – (a) Vigraharaj IV (b) Arnoraj (c) Ajayaraj (d) Prithviraj III (e) Question not attempted Raj. P.C.S. (Pre) 2023 Ans. (a) Vigraharaj IV was the most powerful ruler of the Chauhan dynasty. He conquered the nearby region and increased the boundaries of the empire. He triumphed over the Tomaras and took possession of Eastern Punjab and Delhi. He won over the Muslim ruler of Punjab.

s: Battle that laid the foundation of Muslim domination in India was :
x: The second battle of Tarain was fought between Muhammad Ghori and Rajput army of Prithviraj Chauhan. The battle took place in 1192 AD near Tarain. In this battle, Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by Muhammad Ghori. After this battle, the Muslim power was strongly enrooted in northern India, which may be regarded as a turning point in Indian history.

s: Which one of the following rulers from Central Asia conquered North India in 1192?
x: Shihabuddin Muhammad Ghori, the ruler of Central Asia, conquered north India in 1192 A.D. The first attack of Muhammad Ghori took place in 1175A.D. on Multan. He attacked Multan and Uch in 1175-76 A.D. and Gujarat in 1178 A.D. In 1191 A.D., he fought the first battle of Tarain with Prithviraj Chauhan and was defeated. In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 A.D.), Prithviraj was defeated by Ghori, and in this way, a central Muslim political system was established, which lasted for many years.

s: In which battle Muhammad Ghori defeated Jayachandra-
x: Muhammad Ghori defeated the king of Kannauj, Jayachandra in the battle of Chandawar during 1194 A.D. This battle was fought in Chandawar (In Modern Firozabad district in U.P.), on the bank of Yamuna River close to Agra.

s: Who among the following rulers is famous as ‘Prithviraj Chauhan’?

s: Who among the following Rajput Kings defeated Muhammad Ghori for the first time?
x: Ghori's first defeat (1178) was at the hands of the Gujarat Chaulukya/Solanki ruler Mularaja II (Bhimdev II), the 'Baghel Bhim' of the options, not Prithviraj, who beat him in 1191 but lost in 1192.

s: In which battle did Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori?
x: Prithviraj won the First Battle of Tarain (1191); Ghori won the second (1192) and Chandawar (1194).

s: When was the first battle of Tarain fought?
x: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191, with Prithviraj winning; the second was in 1192.

s: The second battle of Tarain was fought between?
x: The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was fought between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan; Ghori won.

s: Which among the following was the central Asian ruler who conquered North India in 1192 AD?
x: Muhammad Ghori won the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, which opened North India. Mahmud of Ghazni only raided.

s: The battle from which Muslim rule in India established?
x: The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was the turning point: Ghori's victory opened North India to Turkish rule.

s: Coins of which Muslim ruler bear an image of Devi Lakshmi?
x: Coins issued by Ghori have image of Goddess Lakshmi and Kalma was inscribed in Arabic on some other coins.

s: Muhammad Ghori suffered his first defeat at the hands of which ruler?
x: Ghori's first defeat came in 1178 in Gujarat at the hands of Mularaja II (Bhimdev II), a Chaulukya/Solanki ruler, near Mount Abu, before his Tarain battles with Prithviraj.

s: Which slave of Muhammad Ghori conquered Bengal and Bihar –
x: Muhammad Ghori and Aybak didn’t ever think of conquering Bihar and Bengal. This task was accomplished by their ordinary slave Ikhtiyar Uddin Muhammad-Bin-Bakhtiyar Khalji. Between 1193 and 1203 AD, he conquered Bihar and destroyed Vikramshila, Nalanda and captured the capital Odantpur. He attacked Bengal between 1198 and 1204-05, where its ruler Lakshman Sen fled away without fighting in the battlefield. Turkish army entered the capital Nadiya and resorted to massive loot. In the absence of the King, the city surrendered. Lakshman Sen had taken refuge in East Bengal and ruled there for sometime. Bakhtiyar Khalji did not try to conquer the whole of the Bengal. Bakhtiyar Khalji made his capital in Lakhnauti.

s: Who devastated Chola dynasty eventually?
x: The Chola empire was devastated by Malik Kafur, the commander of Alauddin Khalji; Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquests were in Bihar and Bengal.

s: The slave of Muhammad Ghori who conquered Bengal and Bihar was?
x: Bakhtiyar Khalji, Ghori's slave/general, conquered Bihar and Bengal (1193-1203). Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate, and Iltutmish and Yaldauz did not conquer these regions.

x: Several Turkish rulers, including Mahmud of Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori, invaded northern India between the 11th and 12th centuries. Among these, Ghori's invasion had a more significant impact, leading to the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate, which laid the foundation for Muslim rule in India. During this period, the political conditions in India were highly fragmented, with many small and independent states. Due to this lack of unity, it was easy for the invaders to achieve victory and establish control. There was no unified resistance against them. Thus, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A).
